summary: This round correctly closes the three narrow bugs it targets (config-file/env-var cgroup-path override, missing '+' force-push stripping, and single-refspec-only checking on git push), each with a genuine, passing, live-reproduced regression test against the real shipped snippet -- solid, honest, well-tested work as far as it goes. However, the round's headline claim -- that the dual-signal check is now 'kernel-verified' and 'no environment variable or shell builtin lets an ordinary interactive process rewrite its own cgroup path to impersonate a unit it isn't actually running under' -- does not actually hold in this deployment. Per SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md, veridian-worker/veridian-supervisor units run under systemd --user (linger on) owned by the same 'rajat' account that also runs the interactive shell this guard is meant to constrain. That account therefore already has standing authority to run 'systemd-run --user --unit=veridian-worker@x.service ...', which mints a transient unit with a genuine INVOCATION_ID and a genuine /proc/self/cgroup path containing 'veridian-worker@x.service' -- satisfying _interactive_guard_is_real_worker_context()'s unanchored regex with zero file/env spoofing, in one ordinary command. This is a full, standard-tooling bypass of the exact 'is this really a dispatched worker' check that rounds 2 and 3 were built to harden, is not disclosed in the snippet's own known_limitations section, and is not covered by tests/interactive_session_guard_test.sh. Consistent with how rounds 1 and 2 were rejected for comparably real, undisclosed bypasses, this should go back for a round 4 that either closes the gap (e.g. an out-of-band per-task secret/credential the dispatcher injects and the guard checks, rather than relying solely on unit-name pattern matching) or, at minimum, explicitly documents this specific bypass in known_limitations so the guard's guarantees are not overstated.
issues: Dual-signal check bypassable via ordinary 'systemd-run --user --unit=veridian-worker@<anything>.service ...' -- since workers run as systemd --user units under the same account as the interactive shell, that account can mint a transient unit with a genuinely matching INVOCATION_ID and /proc/self/cgroup content with no privilege escalation and no file/env spoofing, fully defeating _interactive_guard_is_real_worker_context() in _lib.sh. Not disclosed in known_limitations, not covered by the test suite.

Secondary, lower-confidence item worth checking in the same follow-up: _interactive_guard_gh_is_merge() only recognizes 'pr merge' when it is literally $1/$2 -- if gh's -R/--repo (or another persistent flag) can legally precede the subcommand in the installed gh version's flag parser, 'gh -R owner/repo pr merge N --merge' would not be recognized as a merge and would pass through unblocked. Should be verified against the actual gh CLI behavior on VERIDIAN-DEV and either confirmed as not applicable or fixed by skipping leading flags before matching subcommand words.
